result_text:
I fixed the four default conventions in `codeanalyzer/src/main/java/nl/obren/sokrates/sourcecode/scoping/ScopingConventions.java`. Nothing is committed.

- **HTML generated pages (3 rules):** `(html|html|xhtml)` is now `(html|htm|xhtml)`, so `.htm` pages match the pkgdown, Doxygen and meta-generator rules.
- **.NET XML doc rule:** `.*/[.]xml` is now `.*[.]xml`, so `MyAssembly.xml` matches. The `<doc>` line check in the first 2 lines still gates it.
- **JavaScript `// Generated by` rule:** `.*/[.]js` is now `.*[.]js`, so `app.js` matches. The first-line content check still gates it.
- **Gradle JavaScript rule:** `.*[.][-]gradle[.]js` is now `.*-gradle[.]js`, so `build-gradle.js` matches.

Existing `.html`, `.xhtml`, `.xml`, `.js` and `build.gradle` coverage is unchanged, and the content checks still keep ordinary hand-written files out.

I did not verify this by running code. No existing tests cover these conventions, so the offline Maven test run had nothing to execute. My attempt to check the regexes directly was blocked (writing a scratch file under `/tmp` was denied). The regexes were checked by reading only.
